message: Running command: cd /tmp && printf '\xfd' > /tmp/poc.bin && xxd /tmp/poc.bin && /tmp/work/meson/fuzzing/fuzz_date_parse /tmp/poc.bin 2>&1 | head -8

message.content:
`g_utf8_get_char` uses `UTF8_GET` which reads `len` bytes. For `\xfd`, `UTF8_COMPUTE` determines `len=5`, but the buffer only has 1 byte. So `UTF8_GET` reads 5 bytes, going past the end of the 2-byte buffer (1 byte + nul terminator). This is the heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.

The root cause: `g_date_set_parse` does not validate that the input is valid UTF-8 before calling `g_utf8_casefold`/`g_utf8_normalize` in `g_date_fill_parse_tokens`. The fix (commit `b4c2e4d553`) added `g_utf8_validate` at the start of `g_date_set_parse`.
